newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures jump sharply late, end firm.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures jump sharply late, end firm.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures rallied late in the session again, rising to new session highs after the close of the stock market to end sharply higher.
Volume was thin, however, on the first session after the Christmas holiday as many participants apparently extended their vacations at least another day.
The late rally today brought March S&P 500s close to a new contract high, a level that some analysts said could be reached in the three trading sessions that remain this year.
"We could make new highs by the end of the year," said Jay Hohmann, head futures trader at Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities. The current contract high in the March S&P contract is 772.40.

Steady Treasury bond futures prices, which some participants linked to early reports that Christmas sales by retailers may not have been all that strong, contributed to the firm tone in index futures during the day.
Still, some traders were skeptical of the advance, especially the higher opening that created a chart gap.

"We gapped open higher (Thursday) on a bunch of nothingness," said one S&P 500 floor broker, noting the opening at 760.00 from Tuesday's settlement at 759.05. Prices later partially filled that gap when the contract slipped to a session low of 759.60.
The S&P premium hovered at wider levels than the theoretical, but only moved above that area -- and to an area where buy programs might be triggered above 7.00 points -- late in the session.
Data to be released Friday include jobless claims for the latest week, expected to slip to 346,000 from 351,000, and November durable goods orders, forecast to rise 0.1 percent.
Nikkei 225 stock index futures managed to end slightly higher, despite sizable losses in the cash Nikkei index overnight.

At settlement, March S&P 500s were up 5.55 points at 764.60, Russell 2000s gained 3.05 points to 363.75, Value Line futures were up 5.70 points to 690.20, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 5.0 to 19,330.0 and Midcap 400s rose 1.55 point to 257.30.
